主要内容: Foreign investors continue to show strong interest in New York City's real estate market, which remains one of the most expensive globally. The city is particularly attractive to buyers from China, Europe, and the Middle East, with specific neighborhoods drawing significant attention. Chinese investors, for instance, are purchasing high-end condos on Fifth Avenue and Park Avenue, as well as in Tribeca and SoHo, according to Carole Armstrong of DJK Residential. Russian and Middle Eastern buyers are also showing interest in luxury areas like Columbus Circle and Central Park West, with Russians drawn to the prestige and reputation of these properties. In Brooklyn, Cobble Hill is a popular choice for French buyers, thanks to its proximity to public transportation and English-French bilingual schools. Midtown, especially Midtown West, remains a favorite for foreign investors due to the availability of affordable, high-quality one-bedroom apartments. The Upper East Side is also a hotspot, particularly for Asian buyers seeking quality schools and stable investments. Overall, the city's real estate market continues to attract a diverse range of international buyers, with specific neighborhoods catering to different investor preferences. Foreign investors are increasingly buying property in New York City, particularly in areas like the North Shore of Staten Island. John Boyd, principal at The Boyd Company, noted that new construction on Staten Island is attracting wealthy foreigners due to the recent ferry service and luxury condominiums. While there was a sharp downturn from China over the last two years, recent months have seen a rise in purchases from the region. Staten Island, which has less cachet than other boroughs, offers good deals for foreign buyers. The Verrazano Narrows Bridge provides a view of the area, highlighting its strategic location. The trend reflects a growing interest in New York City real estate from international investors.
